source_neutral.procedure: The surviving draft is treated as a possibly mixed collection of textual passages, alterations and assembled leaves. Each such unit gets a separately indexed record that preserves its location and its relationships to other units. The working hypothesis is that the draft contains distinguishable revision or assembly contributions; both their existence and their separability are hypotheses, not established facts. The sole starting assumption is that inspection may reveal discriminating variant readings, handwriting features, insertion relationships or paper features. Additional witnesses, dates and provenance are used only if they are available and established. Overall process: a manual worksheet compares the indexed records, in a predefined order, against a fixed panel of documented reference features, iteratively assigning, rejecting, carrying forward and revising associations between records and reference groups until the associations stop changing or the remaining distinctions require unavailable evidence. The resulting association patterns are then interpreted, where independent evidence allows, and candidate sequences of revision and assembly are compared against earlier-than and later-than constraints. The output is a best-supported sequence to the extent the constraints discriminate, otherwise a partial order with competing sequences retained and unresolved relations named.
source_neutral.action: 1. Create separately indexed records for passages, alterations and assembled leaves, preserving locations and relationships. 2. Before each run, define a fixed panel of documented reference features drawn from the draft and any available witnesses, and define the comparison order. 3. Carry the indexed records through the successive comparisons on a manual worksheet. 4. At each comparison: provisionally retain a record's association with a reference group when an explicit feature matches; reject the association when evidence contradicts it; carry unresolved associations forward. 5. Reconsider retained associations against subsequent evidence and drop those that become contradictory. 6. Allow a record to remain associated with several groups. 7. Record matches, contradictions and missing evidence separately. 8. Repeat the comparisons until a full pass changes no associations, or until remaining distinctions require unavailable evidence. 9. Do not count repeated inspection of the same feature as additional support. 10. Where available, use legible deletion and replacement relationships, demonstrable insertion dependencies, physical assembly evidence and securely dated witnesses to set earlier-than and later-than constraints. 11. Compare candidate sequences against those constraints, preferring sequences that explain the supported relations with fewer unsupported revision or assembly events. 12. Keep narrative order distinct from composition order. 13. For disputed comparisons, repeat them with explicitly documented alternative unit boundaries or reference definitions, keeping each run's conditions fixed.
source_neutral.observables: Whether records develop distinct, stable patterns of association with the fixed reference groups. Which features sustain each association. Which comparisons cause an association to be dropped. Which records remain associated with more than one group or remain unresolved. Separately logged matches, contradictions and missing evidence. A single passage may contain several distinguishable alteration records. Worksheet position, comparison order and number of passes are observations about the procedure itself; they are not dates and not measures of elapsed composition time. No particular grouping outcome is assumed in advance. For sequencing: legible deletion and replacement relationships, demonstrable insertion dependencies, physical assembly evidence and securely dated witnesses, where available. For the dependence check: whether the apparent grouping changes under documented alternative boundaries or reference definitions.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: A stable grouping would support the conclusion that there are distinguishable evidence profiles, and would characterize their relative association with the chosen reference features. Those profiles may be identified as revision or assembly contributions only where independent evidence supports that interpretation. Earlier-than and later-than relations are constrained by legible deletion and replacement relationships, demonstrable insertion dependencies, physical assembly evidence and securely dated witnesses, where available. Candidate sequences are compared against those constraints, with preference for sequences that explain the supported relations with fewer unsupported revision or assembly events. Narrative order is not taken as composition order. A best-supported sequence is reported only to the extent the constraints discriminate among alternatives; otherwise a partial order is reported and competing sequences are retained. Group membership alone establishes neither a date, an author nor a revision stage. A local alteration cannot establish the history of the whole draft. Repeated inspection of the same feature does not count as additional support. Procedural quantities (worksheet position, comparison order, pass count) support no conclusion about dates or composition time.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: indexed records of textual passages, alterations and assembled leaves, each with preserved location and relationships; one passage may hold several alteration records. Reference side: a fixed panel of documented reference features, drawn from the draft and any available witnesses, organized into reference groups and fixed before each run together with the comparison order. Relationships between records and reference groups: association provisionally retained, association rejected, association unresolved and carried forward, association later dropped; a record may hold associations with several groups at once. Evidence categories logged separately: matches, contradictions, missing evidence. Hypothesized components: distinguishable revision or assembly contributions, whose existence and separability are hypotheses. Two layers of result: (a) evidence profiles, meaning patterns of association with reference groups; (b) interpretation of profiles as revision or assembly contributions, conditional on independent evidence. Ordering relations: earlier-than and later-than constraints derived from deletion and replacement relationships, insertion dependencies, physical assembly evidence and securely dated witnesses; candidate sequences evaluated against these constraints; narrative order kept separate from composition order. Final products: a best-supported sequence or a partial order with competing sequences, plus a list of unresolved relations and uncertain claims.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: Test dependence on reference selection, unit boundaries and comparison rules by repeating disputed comparisons with explicitly documented alternative boundaries or reference definitions, holding each run's conditions fixed. If a proposed sequence depends on an ambiguous grouping, seek additional witnesses, inspect the relevant material features, or consult available dated correspondence and provenance. If those checks are unavailable or inconclusive, stop at the supported partial order and name the unresolved relations. No further follow-up beyond these steps is specified.
source_neutral.limits: Conditions: additional witnesses, dates and provenance are usable only if available and established; the existence and separability of contributions are hypotheses; reference features and comparison order must be defined before a run and held fixed within it. Limitations: different contributions may share features and remain inseparable; one contribution may vary internally and appear as several groups; handwriting, wording and paper features can be nonspecific; choices of reference features, unit boundaries and comparison rules can change the apparent grouping; group membership alone establishes neither a date, an author nor a revision stage; a local alteration cannot establish the whole draft's history; worksheet position, comparison order and pass count are not dates or measures of composition time; repeated inspection of the same feature is not additional support; a best-supported sequence is reportable only as far as the constraints discriminate among alternatives. The procedure is a qualitative comparison; it is not a validated separation method and not a calibrated chronology. Stopping rules: end the comparison cycle when a full pass changes no associations, or when the remaining distinctions require unavailable evidence. If checks on an ambiguous grouping are unavailable or inconclusive, stop at the supported partial order and name the unresolved relations.
